content.user_title: Estimate Taiwan Labor and Health Insurance Costs
content.value_statement: Taiwan payroll deductions depend on separate insurance salary tiers and dependent counts. This skill estimates employee premiums and employer pension contributions using its documented 2026 tables.
actual_capabilities: Select labor, health, and pension salary tiers by rounding salaries upward to the next tier, subject to each table's cap.
Estimate employee labor and employment insurance premiums using the documented combined 12.5% rate and 20% employee share.
Estimate employee health premiums using a 5.17% rate, a 30% employee share, and up to three insured dependents.
Calculate employer pension contributions at 6% of the selected pension wage tier, capped at TWD 150,000.
Round monetary amounts to whole dollars with Decimal arithmetic and present a breakdown with the applicable year and estimate label.
Provide government source links and embedded calculation assertions without requiring API keys or network access for the arithmetic.
limitations: Tables cover 2026 only; later years require checking official announcements and updating the embedded values.
Part-time workers, union members, self-employed people, foreign migrant workers, and workers outside the stated age eligibility are outside scope.
Occupational accident insurance, supplementary health premiums, and employer labor and health insurance shares are not calculated.
The calculation function lacks input validation; confirm a valid monthly salary and a nonnegative whole-number dependent count before estimating.

use_cases.title: Review Monthly Deductions
use_cases.description: Estimate employee insurance deductions from monthly salary and dependent count, then compare the breakdown with a payslip.

use_cases.title: Prepare Payroll Estimates
use_cases.description: Check salary tier selection and employer pension contributions for ordinary full-time employees using the documented 2026 rules.

use_cases.title: Compare Salary Offers
use_cases.description: Compare employee insurance deductions across proposed salaries while keeping employer pension contributions separate from employee deductions.
use_cases.target_user: Job seekers comparing Taiwan employment offers

prompt_templates.title: Estimate One Salary
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate my 2026 Taiwan insurance deductions for a monthly salary of TWD 50,000 and no insured dependents. Show the salary tiers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: estimate a single eligible employee's monthly deductions.

prompt_templates.title: Include Dependents
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate 2026 employee premiums for TWD 50,000 monthly salary and one insured dependent. Separate employee deductions from employer pension contributions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: include family coverage in the premium estimate.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Salary Tiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare 2026 deductions for monthly salaries of TWD 30,000, 50,000, and 60,000 with two insured dependents. Explain tier selection and caps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare salaries across different insurance tier boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Payroll Estimate
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a 2026 payroll estimate for TWD 50,000 salary, one dependent, TWD 1,145 labor premium, and TWD 1,570 health premium. Show calculations. Separate employer pension contributions and list excluded charges. Cite the supplied official references and identify assumptions requiring confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review a payroll breakdown without treating an estimate as an official assessment.

output_examples.input: Estimate 2026 premiums for TWD 50,000 monthly salary and one insured dependent.
output: 2026 estimate for an eligible full-time employee.
Labor insured salary: TWD 45,800. Employee labor and employment insurance premium: TWD 1,145.
Health insured amount: TWD 50,600. Employee health premium including one dependent: TWD 1,570.
Total estimated employee insurance deductions: TWD 2,715 per month.
Employer pension contribution: TWD 3,036 per month, separate from employee deductions.
Employer insurance shares, occupational accident insurance, and supplementary premiums are excluded.

output_examples.input: Estimate 2026 premiums for TWD 29,500 monthly salary and three insured dependents.
output: 2026 estimate for an eligible full-time employee.
Labor and health salary tiers: TWD 29,500.
Employee labor and employment insurance premium: TWD 738.
Health premium per insured person: TWD 458. Employee plus three dependents: TWD 1,832.
Total estimated employee insurance deductions: TWD 2,570 per month.
Employer pension contribution: TWD 1,770 per month, separate from employee deductions.

best_practices: Confirm the applicable year, employment eligibility, total monthly wage, and nonnegative whole-number dependent count before calculating.
Check official BLI and NHI announcements before using another year's rates or relying on estimates for payroll decisions.
Report selected tiers and rounded amounts separately, label results as estimates, and distinguish employee deductions from employer pension contributions.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse the embedded 2026 tables for other years without checking official announcements.
Do not apply these formulas to excluded worker groups or treat the result as a complete employer payroll cost.
Do not supply identity numbers, login credentials, or unrelated personal records; salary and dependent count are sufficient for the estimate.

faq.question: Does the calculation require an API key or internet access?
faq.answer: No API key is required. The embedded Python arithmetic runs offline; checking current government announcements requires internet access.

faq.question: Which year do the embedded tables cover?
faq.answer: They cover 2026, also called ROC year 115. Verify official announcements before using the skill for another year.

faq.question: How are salary tiers selected?
faq.answer: Each table selects the smallest tier at or above the monthly salary. Salaries above a table's maximum use its highest tier.

faq.question: How many dependents affect health premiums?
faq.answer: The employee pays for themselves plus up to three insured dependents. Additional dependents do not increase this calculation.

faq.question: Is the employer pension contribution deducted from employee pay?
faq.answer: No. The skill reports the employer's 6% pension contribution separately from the employee's insurance deductions.

faq.question: Does this provide an official or complete payroll assessment?
faq.answer: No. It provides estimates for eligible full-time employees and excludes employer insurance shares, occupational accident insurance, and supplementary premiums.
